key_insight: Phase-adapted shallow neural dictionaries achieve N^(-1/2) Sobolev approximation bounds, with phase matching reducing the bound’s growth for chirped signals.
engineering_relevance: Matching neural dictionary phases to oscillatory targets can improve approximation guarantees without changing the dictionary-size convergence rate.
method: Define weighted STSAFT-modulation spaces via chirp correspondence with classical modulation spaces.
Construct a transform-adapted neural dictionary and prove bounded-domain and global approximation bounds.
Analyze how dictionary–target phase mismatch affects upper bounds for fixed-scale chirp families.
evidence_signal: Four numerical experiments examine model comparison, dictionary-size error decay, phase mismatch, and restricted-translation obstruction, separately from theoretical best-approximation estimates.
watch_item: Global guarantees require unrestricted translations; phase-mismatch comparisons concern upper bounds, not thresholds for optimal approximation error.
paper_title: Weighted STSAFT-Modulation Spaces and Approximation by Phase-Adapted Neural Networks
